title: Lasagne al Forno
subtitle: Classic baked lasagne with ragù and béchamel
excerpt: Layers of fresh pasta, slow-cooked beef ragù, and a rich béchamel, baked until the top is golden and bubbling. The assembly is straightforward; the ragù needs a proper two-hour cook.

recipe.sourceNotes: Lasagne al forno, in its original Bolognese form, uses egg pasta sheets, ragù alla bolognese, and béchamel. The version spread globally by Italian immigrants during the twentieth century became the world's most recognisable baked pasta dish. This recipe follows the Emilian approach: short ragù cook time compared to the full bolognese, but layered with the proper béchamel.

recipeTools.notes: A 30 x 20 cm deep baking dish.

content.text: Lasagne al forno has three separate preparations that come together in the dish: the ragù, the béchamel, and the pasta. The ragù should be slightly wetter than you would use for tagliatelle, it will dry out somewhat in the oven. The béchamel should be thick enough to not run but still pourable. The pasta, if dried, should be par-cooked before layering; fresh sheets go in raw.

Make the ragù: heat the oil in a heavy pot. Cook the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic for 10 minutes until soft. Add the mince, turn up the heat, and brown thoroughly, 8 minutes. Add the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and reduce by half. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, and bay leaves. Season and simmer, partially covered, for 1.5 hours until rich and thick. Remove the bay leaves.

Make the béchamel: melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 2 minutes. Off the heat, whisk in the milk gradually. Return to the heat and stir constantly until thick. Season with salt, pepper, and half the parmesan.
Heat the oven to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. If using dried pasta, par-cook in salted boiling water for 4 minutes, then lay on clean tea towels.

Assemble: spread a thin layer of béchamel over the base of the dish. Add a layer of pasta sheets, then ragù, then béchamel. Repeat layers, finishing with béchamel. Scatter the remaining parmesan over the top.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is golden and the edges are bubbling. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting, it will hold its shape better and be easier to serve.
